route_name: pbmix: trees as mixtures of shifted Poisson-binomial laws, conditioning on a set B with T - B a linear forest
target_lemma:
Setup (exact identity, holds for every tree). Take B ⊆ V(T) with T - B a linear forest: the branch set {deg>=3}, or a bipartition class. For each independent σ ⊆ B, a^σ(x) = x^{|σ|} Q_σ(x), where Q_σ is the product of the path polynomials of T - B - N(σ). Q_σ is real-rooted, so each normalised term is a shifted Poisson-binomial (PB) law, and I(T;x) = f = Σ_σ a^σ. Fix k. Put π(σ) = a^σ_k/f_k (the law of S∩B for a uniform k-independent set S), u_σ = a^σ_{k+1}/a^σ_k and v_σ = a^σ_{k-1}/a^σ_k. Collect the support-boundary components (a^σ_k = 0) in β_± = Σ a^σ_{k±1}/f_k. Then δ_k(f) := 1 - f_{k-1}f_{k+1}/f_k^2 = 1 - (E_π u + β_+)(E_π v + β_-), and δ^σ = 1 - u_σ v_σ. In the bulk case this is δ_k(f) = C_k - S_k, with C_k = E_π[u]·E_π[δ^σ/u] (component curvature) and S_k = E_π[u]·E_π[1/u] - 1 ≥ 0 (posterior spread of the component log-ratios). Also (k+1-|σ|)u_σ = E_k[#free vertices of T-B | S∩B=σ].

LEMMA PBM(η, c, N1). There are absolute constants η, c > 0 and N1 with the following property. For every tree T on n ≥ N1 vertices and every k with ceil(n/4) ≤ k ≤ q = ceil((2α-1)/3), there is a B (the branch set, or the better bipartition class) such that:
(L1, component curvature) δ^σ_k ≥ c/V_σ(λ) for every σ in supp π_k with V_σ(λ) ≥ V0, where λ is a tilt placing the component's first descent at k-|σ|. For binomial components the exact value (m+1)/((j+1)(m-j+1)) is used. For path-product components, thm:main plus tilt invariance gives c = 1/4; the data need c ≳ 0.4 for dense-branch trees with B = branch set.
(L2, spread budget) S_k + (boundary terms) ≤ (1-η)·E_π[u]·E_π[(c/V_σ)/u].
Conclusion: i_k^2 > i_{k-1} i_{k+1} on the window. Heuristic (validated numerically, float diagnostic): the mixture loss ρ_k := 1 - δ_k(f)/E_π[δ^σ] ≈ the between-variance fraction Var(E[X|σ_B])/Var(X) at tilt λ = f_k/f_{k+1}. So (L2) amounts to "the within-component variance fraction is at least η0, and the posterior law of the B-configuration given |S| = k contracts at scale sqrt(V_within)".
how_it_closes:
Lemma PBM gives strict log-concavity at every k in [ceil(n/4), q] for all trees with n ≥ N1. Fang et al. Prop 8.2 (arXiv:2609.20961, p. 15, eq. (8.8)) gives i_0 ≤ ... ≤ i_{ceil(n/4)}. The bipartite Levit–Mandrescu tail (eq. (8.9), same page) gives nonincreasing from q. The window is nonempty since α ≥ n/2, and log-concavity on it makes the ratios i_k/i_{k-1} nonincreasing for ceil(n/4) ≤ k ≤ q+1. That is the same patching as their proof of Theorem 1.1 (p. 16), so the sequence is unimodal. Exhaustive verification through n = 32 would close the gap only if N1 ≤ 33, which this route will not deliver.

N1 has not been computed, and no value or order is claimed. The proof shape makes N1 depend on three constants: (i) V0 in the bulk-PB lemma (L1); (ii) a lower bound η0(λ) on the within-component variance fraction at fugacities up to the one placing the mean at q (Fang use λ ∈ [1/4, 12]); (iii) the Kolmogorov-distance accuracy ε ≈ c·η0^{3/2} that (L2) needs from an effective CLT for the B-configuration statistic. Heuristically N1 ≈ (C_BE/(c·η0^{3/2}))^{2/γ}, where C_BE and γ are the constant and rate of the available effective CLT. Fang's Section 5 rate O(b/√n + b^{(a-1)/2} + ...) with an unspecified a < 1 suggests γ could be small and N1 very large.

kill_test:
Pre-registered criteria, stated before the runs. KT-a: the form of the route that uses thm:main as the component-curvature input is dead on a family if the certificate cert_k = 1 - (E_π u + β_+)(E_π[(1-d_σ)/u] + β_-) fails inside the window [ceil(n/4), q] and ρ_k does not decrease with n. KT-b: the route is dead in every form if ρ_k → 1 under every tested B (branch set, both bipartition classes, non-leaves). Here d_σ is the PB bound 1/(4V_σ(λ)) at a tilt with first descent at k-|σ|, evaluated exactly at the closure endpoints, with the Newton/ULC bound as fallback only when V < 1.

Every inequality is computed in exact int/Fraction arithmetic, and every decomposition asserts Σ_σ a^σ = I(T) against the tree DP.

Tests, in the order to run them: (1) complete binary trees with B = degree-3 vertices, a scalable bivariate (s,m) DP because the components are binomials; (2) the same trees with B = each bipartition class; (3) the census of all trees n ≤ 15 with B = branch set; (4) spiders, random trees and combs; (5) an adversarial hill-climb maximising ρ over trees at n = 22.

What would kill the route: KT-a firing on a family whose ρ is flat or rising, or KT-b (ρ → 1 for every B).
kill_test_result:
KT-a FIRED; KT-b did NOT fire.

(a) Complete binary trees, B = degree-3 vertices, window [ceil(n/4), q]. The PB-bound certificate fails at 3/7 (n=31), 5/13 (n=63) and 11/26 (n=127) window indices, always in the upper window. Max ρ is 0.3068, 0.3049, 0.3371: not decreasing. Failures begin where ρ exceeds about 0.22, as the 1/4 constant predicts. LC itself holds at every index. These components are binomials whose exact curvature certifies LC, so the failure belongs to the proven constant, not to log-concavity. The same trees with B = non-leaves fail 3/7, 5/13, 12/26 (ρ max 0.345). Random trees with B = non-leaves (n=40, 80; 6 trees) fail 51/53 pairs (ρ up to 0.409).

(b) B = branch set on path-heavy trees: PB certificate passes everywhere, and the PB bound is operative on 100% of posterior bulk mass. Spiders (7 shapes, n = 21..201; 61 pairs): ρ ≤ 0.0042. Random n = 30, 40, 50 (8 trees; 48 pairs): ρ ≤ 0.0976. Sparse combs L = 20, 26 (21 pairs): ρ ≤ 0.1703.

(c) Census of all 13,163 trees n = 8..15 with B = branch set (39,576 (tree,k) pairs): LC fails 0; PB-bound-with-ULC-fallback certificate fails 44 (2 at n=13, 8 at n=14, 34 at n=15); max(PB, ULC) certificate fails 0; max ρ = 0.3026. The small-n passes are largely ULC-driven.

(d) B = the better bipartition class (binomial components, exact curvature, the PB theorem is not needed): max ρ is 0.173/0.192/0.168/0.178 on CBT d = 3..6, 0.276/0.262/0.332 on random n = 40/80/120, and ≤ 0.328 on combs. The worse class reaches 0.92.

(e) Hill-climb at n = 22 (|B| ≤ 10, 200 s): converged to cubic trees with ρ = 0.3127 at k = q (PB certificate fails there; ULC certificate passes; LC holds). No family pushed the best-B loss toward 1. Max best-B ρ ≤ 0.34 in all runs.

(f) Heuristic check (float diagnostic, 816 rows): ρ_k exceeded the between-variance fraction in 119 rows, by at most 0.050 (n=7), and by at most 0.005 for n ≥ 120.

Not completed: CBT depth 7 (n=255) was stopped at about 16 minutes under the compute cap. Certificates were not computed for random n = 120, 160 or for the combs with B = non-leaves.
main_obstacle:
1. The proven PB constant is too small for dense branching. When T has Θ(n) branch vertices (complete binary trees, cubic trees), the branch-set B carries a between-variance fraction of about 0.3. The mixture loss ρ then exceeds 1/4, and V·δ ≥ 1/4 cannot pay for it. There are two escapes, and neither uses thm:main as proved: (a) a new two-sided bulk PB lemma, V·δ_j ≥ c for |j - mean| ≤ K sqrt(V) with c ≳ 0.4 (pure PB, formalizable, plausibly provable by Edgeworth/saddle-point, but not in hand; prop:one-third shows c ≤ 1/3 at V = 1, so V → ∞ must be used); or (b) choose B as a bipartition class. Then the components are binomials with exact curvature, and the PB margin theorem drops out of the route entirely.

2. The real core is (L2), and it is an effective CLT in disguise. Bounding the posterior spread S_k requires the conditional law of the B-configuration statistic given |S| = k to contract at scale sqrt(V_within). That holds if the shift law is approximately Gaussian at that scale (then ρ ≈ b²/(b²+V_w) < 1). It fails if the shift law is far from log-concave there. No elementary argument was found.

The structural gain is narrow. Because the PB/binomial components smooth at width sqrt(V_w) ≍ sqrt(n), (L2) needs only Kolmogorov-distance closeness at a fixed accuracy ε(η0) ≈ c·η0^{3/2}, which is what a Raič-type Berry–Esseen delivers directly. Fang et al.'s Prop. 6.2 additionally needs characteristic-function convergence uniform on compacts, the Fourier tail bound (Lemma 6.1) and dominated convergence. That is a real reduction in what must be made explicit, not a way around the CLT. The route inherits their Section 5 CLT with its unspecified O-constants and unspecified a < 1, so N1 is likely still very large.

3. Cross-connection. Fang's Lemma 6.1 conditions on one side of a bipartition, which leaves independent Bernoullis on the other side: exactly this route's bipartition-class binomial mixture, read through Fourier. The exact identity δ = C - S is the non-Fourier form of the same decomposition. An effective version might come from making their Section 5 CLT explicit and feeding it into (L2) instead of Prop. 6.2. Not checked.

No outward literature search was run in this lane (inward grep of notes/ for 'poisson', 'mixture', 'real-rooted', 'claw', 'hub set', 'branch vertices', 'degree >= 3', plus the notes listed). So no claim is made about whether effective CLTs for hard-core functionals exist in the literature.
